sections.content: How many people are "collector salespersons and credit agents"?

5,360 people

were counted on the census as "collector salespersons and credit agents" in England and Wales in March 2021.

This makes this type of work the ninth least common occupation reported on the census.

Collector salespersons and credit agents visit private households to obtain orders and collect payments for goods and services.

People who had this job were generally similar in age to the working population

The occupation of "collector salespersons and credit agents" had a similar age profile compared with the whole working population.

The largest age group of people who had this job were those aged 25 to 29 years. Of the whole working population 11.1% were aged 25 to 29 years. For people working as "collector salespersons and credit agents", 13.7% were in this age group.

The age group with the smallest proportion of people working as "collector salespersons and credit agents" was 16 to 19 years.

sections.content:
Other jobs that had a similar age profile to "collector salespersons and credit agents" included:

  • vehicle technicians, mechanics and electricians
  • engineering technicians
  • delivery operatives

Select your age group to see the ten most popular occupations for your age

More women than men had this job

Among people working as "collector salespersons and credit agents" there were more women than men (58.4% compared with 41.6%).

This means "collector salespersons and credit agents" had a similar proportion of men and women compared with the wider occupation group it falls within of "sales occupations".

Men made up 41.6% and women made up 58.4% of "collector salespersons and credit agents"
Across the whole working population, 52% were men and 48% were women. This occupation was one of the jobs for which the proportion of men and women was closest to this overall picture.

Other jobs that had a similar proportion of men and women to "collector salespersons and credit agents" included:

  • marketing and commercial managers
  • environmental health professionals
  • business associate professionals (other)

These are the occupations for which the proportion of men and women was most equally split:

  • quality assurance and regulatory professionals
  • chartered and certified accountants
  • conservation professionals

We can look at who worked as "collector salespersons and credit agents" by age group and for men and women at the same time to see how these two factors interact.

Men and women with this occupation had a similar age profile, as shown in the chart below.

The percentage of men and women who are "collector salespersons and credit agents" across age groups

How many people do this job by disability status, employment type and area

Of people working as "collector salespersons and credit agents", 14.3% were disabled. This means people said they had a long-term condition that limited them "a little" or "a lot" in their day-to-day activities. The average for all occupations is 9.6%.

Disability is more common among people who are older. This occupation had a similar age profile compared with the whole working population.

People with this job were more likely to work full-time than part-time (58.4% compared with 41.6%).

They are also more likely to be an employee (64.8%) than self-employed (35.2%).

The region of England and Wales with the highest percentage of people with this job was the South East. At a local level, the areas with the highest percentage of people in this occupation included Birmingham, this is in the region of the West Midlands.
